- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10) and prices are trending up, model often overcorrects downward — adjust forecast upward to avoid premature reversal.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the next 5–7 days — reduce forecast slope to prevent overcorrection.  
- Model consistently underestimates mean reversion in 10–15 day horizons — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if recent 7-day average is above 30-day moving average.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.10+), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting.  
- In 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price action — apply 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
